## Conclusion

The authors' research with Puppet revealed breakthrough relationships between delivery performance, technical practices, cultural norms, and organizational performance. Since nearly every company relies on software, delivery performance is critical to any organization today—regardless of size or industry vertical—affected by leadership, tools, automation, and a culture of continuous learning and improvement.

Part I presents research showing how software delivery performance drives organizational outcomes: commercial measures like profitability, productivity, and market share, as well as noncommercial measures like efficiency, effectiveness, customer satisfaction, and achieving mission goals. Delivering quality software at high tempo with stability is a key value driver and differentiator for all organizations. Part II covers the science behind the research, including design decisions and analysis methods providing the scientific basis for results. Part III addresses organizational change management, with contributions from Steve Bell and Karen Whitley Bell presenting one view of what following these capabilities looks like and what it can provide for innovative organizations.

The research identified key capabilities that contribute to software delivery performance in statistically significant and meaningful ways. High performance cannot be purchased or copied—it requires sustained effort, investment, focus, and time to develop capabilities suited to your specific context and goals. Transformation that so many others have implemented with great success in their own teams and organizations is possible. The findings are unequivocal: the results are worth it.

## Conclusion

The authors reflect on years of surveying technology professionals and producing State of DevOps Reports with Puppet, revealing insights into high-performing teams and organizations. Their research encompasses technology transformations and peer-reviewed publications, demonstrating that software delivery performance is critical for nearly all modern companies. This performance is shaped by leadership, tools, automation, and a culture of continuous learning and improvement.

The book is organized into three parts: Part I establishes why software delivery performance drives organizational outcomes including profitability, productivity, market share, efficiency, effectiveness, customer satisfaction, and mission achievement. Part II details the research methodology, design decisions, and analysis methods. Part III addresses organizational change management, with contributions from Steve Bell and Karen Whitley Bell on transformation implementation.

The authors emphasize that high performance cannot be purchased or replicated—it must be cultivated through sustained effort, investment, focus, and time. Their research demonstrates that these investments yield unequivocal results. The authors hope readers can identify opportunities to enhance their technology and business processes, work culture, and improvement cycles. The book concludes with best wishes for readers' improvement journeys and anticipation of hearing their success stories.
